index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure illustrates the structure of a CNN-based calibrator, denoted as C_w, which processes an input η to produce an output z. The global layout is a horizontal flow diagram enclosed within a light yellow rectangular box, representing the entire calibrator network. The workflow proceeds from left to right, starting with the input η on the far left and ending with the output z on the far right. The network consists of P sequential layers, labeled Layer #1 through Layer #P at the bottom of the diagram, indicating a deep architecture with multiple stages.

Each layer is visually represented as a vertical stack of three 3D rectangular blocks, colored in shades of beige and light brown, with a slight 3D perspective. From top to bottom, these blocks correspond to the operations: Convolution (ConV), Batch Normalization (BN), and Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU). The first layer (Layer #1) contains only ConV and BN, omitting ReLU, while all subsequent layers (Layer #2 to Layer #P) include all three components. The ReLU activation is explicitly labeled beneath the BN block in each of these later layers.

The connections between layers are shown using solid blue arrows pointing rightward, indicating the forward propagation of data. Between Layer #2 and Layer #p, and again between Layer #p and Layer #P-1, dotted blue arrows are used to indicate the continuation of the sequence, suggesting that the number of intermediate layers is variable and not fully drawn. The final layer (Layer #P) ends with a solid blue arrow leading to the output z.

The entire network is labeled C_w at the top center, signifying the calibrator function. The input η is marked on the left with a bold blue arrow entering the first layer, and the output z is marked on the right with a bold blue arrow exiting the last layer. The visual design emphasizes modularity and repetition, with each layer being structurally similar except for the absence of ReLU in the first layer. The consistent use of color, shape, and labeling ensures clarity in identifying the components and their order within the network.
